pr.title: feat(gemm): offer Cake as the last autotuning candidate for bmm_bf16, svdquant and per-token mm_fp4
pr.body:
## 📌 Description

`bmm_bf16`, `mm_nvfp4_svdquant` (SM100/SM103) and the per-token-alpha path of `mm_fp4` already have a Cake backend, but `backend="auto"` never considers it. This PR adds Cake as the **last** runner in their autotuning candidate lists. Under `flashinfer.autotune()`, Cake is profiled with the other runners and used only when it measures fastest. Untuned behavior stays the same.

**Behavior guarantees**

- **Default and fallback stay the same.** Cake is last, so it never becomes the untuned default or the cache-miss fallback. On a miss, AutoTuner falls back to `runners[0]` with tactic -1. On a tie (or within an optional `tie_tolerance`), the earlier runner wins.
- **Cake is offered only for inputs it serves.** The runner set is decided per autotuner bucket: every M that maps to the same tuning-cache key gets the same runners. A cached Cake winner therefore can't be replayed for an M that Cake can't serve. For `mm_fp4`, the Cake runner also requires N >= 32 and 16-byte alignment.
- **Untuned calls keep main's runner list and host cost.** Outside tuning, Cake is listed only when the autotuner could actually select it:
  - it holds a Cake result tuned in this process or loaded from a config file, or
  - an `autotune_v2` store is active.

  This check is the new `AutoTuner.may_select_runner_class(name)`. It is cached through a generation counter that the winner-source dicts bump.
- **Explicit `backend="cake"` is unchanged.** The per-token `mm_fp4` Cake backend is still experimental. `auto` offers it only when `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1` is set.
- **Group tuning lists no Cake.** While tuning under an autotune process group (`set_autotune_process_group`), the three APIs do not list Cake, so every rank builds the same runner list as on `main`.
- **Stream-K scratch is per stream.** The per-token NVFP4 Cake GEMM now takes its Stream-K partials and generation flags from the current stream's scratch (`_get_stream_cache_buf`, as the other `mm_fp4` workspaces do), so concurrent launches on different streams no longer share them. Under CUDA Graph capture each launch gets its own scratch from the graph's pool, with the zero fill of the flags recorded in the same graph, so captured graphs replay correctly in any order. This also applies to explicit `backend="cake"`. The captured fill costs about 1.7 µs per replay on B200 for 2048×7168×16384 (79.3 → 81.0 µs, fresh-process runs) and nothing measurable for 2048×28672×8192; eager launches are unchanged.
- **Kill switch:** `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_CAKE_AUTO_CANDIDATES=1` removes all automatic Cake candidates.
- **No change on SM107 (sm_107a).** The Cake backends for these APIs support only SM100/SM103, so Cake is never offered there.

**Changes** (13 files, +3240/-71)

- `flashinfer/autotuner/autotuner.py`: adds `may_select_runner_class` and the generation counter.
- `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py`, `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_svdquant.py`: add Cake as the last candidate, with the per-bucket offer rule.
- `flashinfer/api_logging.py`: `cake_auto_candidates_enabled()`.
- `docs/autotuning.rst`: new section, "Cake Backends as Autotuning Candidates".
- `flashinfer/experimental/cake_nvfp4_per_token/auto_candidate.py` (new): the operand check and `fp4_gemm` runner of the automatic per-token `mm_fp4` Cake candidate, reached from `gemm_base.py` through a deferred import. `README.md` and `__init__.py` of that package note this.
- `flashinfer/experimental/cake_nvfp4_per_token/cake_backend.py`: Stream-K scratch per stream.
- `docs/development/environment_variables.md`: documents `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_CAKE_AUTO_CANDIDATES`.
- `tests/gemm/test_cake_mm_fp4.py`: also tests the per-stream Stream-K scratch, concurrent launches on two streams, and captured graphs replayed in reverse order and concurrently.
- `tests/gemm/test_cake_mm_fp4.py`: renames `test_cake_is_registered_but_never_auto_selected` to `test_cake_is_registered_as_experimental_backend`.
- New tests: `tests/gemm/test_cake_autotune_candidates_gemm.py`, `tests/gemm/test_cake_autotune_candidates_svdquant.py`.

### Performance

A/B against upstream `main` at the PR base commit (b7a92c0e), on the same node and the same GPU types.

- **Tuning:** each shape gets a fresh AutoTuner and one call under `autotune(True)`, with the call's own M as the only tuning bucket. `backend="auto"` is then timed outside the context.
- **Timing:** CUPTI kernel span over CUDA-graph replay, with an L2 flush before each iteration. Each run takes the median of 3 interleaved repetitions. Each tree (`main` and PR) gets 3 runs on separate GPUs, and the tables report the median across runs.
- **Noise and correctness:**
  - Noise is the A/A spread: the largest relative spread across runs of the same tree, with a 1% floor. A row is marked faster or slower only when the difference exceeds that noise.
  - Tuned output was checked against untuned output in every PR run, and all checks passed.
- **Shapes:** the `bmm_bf16`, `mm_fp4` and svdquant grids from the existing tests, plus model shapes. That gives 28 bmm, 17 `mm_fp4` and 32 svdquant shapes per GPU.
  - On VR200, 15 per-token `mm_fp4` shapes and 2 fp16 bmm shapes raise errors on both `main` and the PR, so they are listed as not measured. The `mm_fp4` shapes fail because SM107 has no suitable `auto` backend for per-token `mm_fp4`. The fp16 bmm shapes fail because the cuDNN fp16 plan build fails.

Geomean latency, PR/`main` (lower is faster):

- **B200:** `bmm_bf16` 0.865, svdquant 0.884, `mm_fp4` 1.002
- **GB300:** `bmm_bf16` 0.876, svdquant 0.908, `mm_fp4` 0.950
- **VR200:** 1.002 / 0.999 / 0.993. This is a no-change control, since Cake is never offered on SM107.

Every slower row had a non-Cake winner in the PR runs, and the candidate set was otherwise identical. These rows reflect tuner selection noise, not Cake. No row where Cake was chosen is slower than `main`.

+def _spy_choose_one(monkeypatch, force_last: bool = False) -> list:
+    """Record every AutoTuner.choose_one call; ``force_last`` returns the last
+    runner with its default tactic instead of the tuner's choice."""
+    calls = []
+    original = AutoTuner.choose_one
+
+    def spy(self, custom_op, runners, tuning_config, inputs, **kwargs):
+        if force_last:
+            runner, tactic = runners[-1], -1
+        else:
+            runner, tactic = original(
+                self, custom_op, runners, tuning_config, inputs, **kwargs
+            )
+        calls.append(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                op=custom_op,
+                runners=[type(r).__name__ for r in runners],
+                runner=type(runner).__name__,
+                is_first=runner is runners[0],
+                tactic=tactic,

+    that its autotune-group plan check compares across ranks (``planned``).
+    The check raises _GroupPlanChecked instead of running a collective; a call
+    without a group returns runners[0] with its default tactic."""

+    choose_one = AutoTuner.choose_one
+
+    def check(phase, selection=(), error=None):

+        planned.append(list(selection[2]))

+
+    def spy(self, custom_op, runners, tuning_config, inputs, **kwargs):

+            return runners[0], -1

+    monkeypatch.setattr(autotuner_module, "_check_tuning_group_phase", check)

+def _dequantize(fp4, sf):
+    """FP32 dequantisation of packed E2M1 + swizzled 128x4 E4M3 scales (rows x K)."""
+    fp4 = fp4.view(torch.uint8)
+    rows, kh = fp4.shape
+    k = 2 * kh
+    e2m1 = torch.tensor(
+        [0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0.0, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6],
+        device=fp4.device,
+    )
+    nib = torch.stack([fp4 & 0xF, fp4 >> 4], dim=-1).reshape(rows, k).long()
+    sf_logical = cb.unswizzle_sf_128x4(sf.view(torch.uint8), rows, k)
+    scales = sf_logical.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()
+    return (e2m1[nib].view(rows, k // 16, 16) * scales[:, :, None]).view(rows, k)
+
+
+def _assert_matches(out, ref):
+    got = out.float()
+    err = (got - ref).abs()
+    ulp = ref.abs() * (2.0**-8 if out.dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 2.0**-11)
+    bound = 1e-2 + 1e-2 * ref.abs() + ulp
+    assert torch.isfinite(got).all()
+    bad = int((err > bound).sum())
+    assert bad == 0, f"{bad} elements exceed |ref| * 1e-2 + 1e-2 + half ulp"
+

+def _fp4_case(m, n=FP4_N, k=FP4_K, seed=0):
+    """NVFP4 operands with a per-token alpha that differs on every row, and the
+    FP32 product of the dequantized operands scaled by it."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    a = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=g)
+    b = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=g)
+    g_in = (448 * 6) / a.float().abs().max()
+    g_w = (448 * 6) / b.float().abs().max()
+    a_fp4, a_sf = nvfp4_quantize(
+        a, g_in, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4, do_shuffle=False
+    )
+    b_fp4, b_sf = nvfp4_quantize(
+        b, g_w, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4, do_shuffle=False
+    )
+    row = 0.25 + torch.arange(m, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) / m
+    alpha = (row / (g_in * g_w)).float().contiguous()
+    ref = (_dequantize(a_fp4, a_sf) @ _dequantize(b_fp4, b_sf).T) * alpha[:, None]
+    return (a_fp4, b_fp4, a_sf, b_sf, alpha), ref
+

+def _mm_fp4(operands, out_dtype, backend="auto", alpha=None, **kwargs):
+    a_fp4, b_fp4, a_sf, b_sf, per_token_alpha = operands
+    return mm_fp4(
+        a_fp4,
+        b_fp4.T,
+        a_sf,
+        b_sf.T,
+        per_token_alpha if alpha is None else alpha,
+        out_dtype,
+        None,
+        block_size=16,
+        use_8x4_sf_layout=False,
+        backend=backend,
+        use_nvfp4=True,
+        **kwargs,
+    )

+def _fp4_runner_inputs(operands, out):
+    a_fp4, b_fp4, a_sf, b_sf, alpha = operands
+    workspace = torch.empty(1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    return [a_fp4, b_fp4.T, a_sf, b_sf.T, alpha, out.dtype, out, 16, True, workspace]

+def _bmm_case(b, m, n, k, seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    a = torch.randn((b, m, k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=g)
+    mat2 = torch.randn(
+        (b, n, k), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=g
+    ).transpose(-2, -1)
+    return a, mat2, torch.bmm(a.float(), mat2.float())

+        tuning_config,

+def _run(p, use_bias, backend="auto", **kwargs):
+    return mm_nvfp4_svdquant(
+        p["xq"],
+        p["wq"],
+        p["x_sf_flat"],
+        p["w_sf_flat"],
+        p["alpha"],
+        p["d"],
+        p["l1_scaled"],
+        bias=p["bias"] if use_bias else None,
+        backend=backend,
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+
+def _runner_inputs(p, use_bias, out):
+    """The ``nvfp4_svdquant_gemm`` runner inputs (no workspace) of ``p``."""
+    return [
+        p["xq"],
+        p["wq"],
+        p["x_sf_flat"],
+        p["w_sf_flat"],
+        p["alpha"],
+        p["d"],
+        p["l1_scaled"],
+        p["bias"] if use_bias else None,
+        out,
+        None,
+    ]
+
+
+def _profile(m):
+    """A tuning profile whose M bucket is ``m`` (all the Cake runner reads)."""
+    return OptimizationProfile(shapes=[[StaticDim(m)]], tensor_initializers=[])
+
+
+def _runner_names(runners):
+    return [type(runner).__name__ for runner in runners]
+
+
+def _expected(p, use_bias):
+    return p["ref_bias"] if use_bias else p["ref"]
+
+
+def _cache_key_ms(m):
+    """Every M that the effective bucket mapping sends to the cache key of ``m``
+    (a plain scan, independent of the module's binary search)."""
+    mapper = AutoTuner.get().get_effective_map_to_tuning_buckets(
+        gemm_svdquant._NVFP4_SVDQUANT_GEMM_TUNING_CONFIG
+    )
+    key = mapper(m)
+    return [x for x in range(1, key + 1) if mapper(x) == key]
+
+
+def _key_admits(m, problem, enable_pdl):
+    """Reference: whether every M of the cache key of ``m`` has a Cake route
+    whose PDL setting admits ``enable_pdl``, checked at every M."""
+    for x in _cache_key_ms(m):
+        route_pdl = gemm_svdquant._cake_nvfp4_svdquant_m_pdl(x, problem)
+        if route_pdl is None or (enable_pdl is not None and enable_pdl != route_pdl):
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _problem_inputs(m, n, k, rank, use_bias):
+    p = _make_gemm_problem(m, n, k, rank=rank)
+    out = torch.empty(m, n, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    return p, _runner_inputs(p, use_bias, out)

+def test_autotuned_auto_is_accurate(
+    monkeypatch, svdquant_choices, m, n, k, rank, use_bias
+):
+    _skip_unless_cake_backend()
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    p = _make_gemm_problem(m, n, k, rank=rank)
+    expected = _expected(p, use_bias)
+    # (runner class, profiled M) of every measurement, timed as usual.
+    profiled = []
+    profile_single_kernel = AutoTuner._profile_single_kernel
+
+    def recording(self, runner, inputs, *args, **kwargs):
+        profiled.append((type(runner).__name__, int(inputs[0].shape[0])))
+        return profile_single_kernel(self, runner, inputs, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(AutoTuner, "_profile_single_kernel", recording)
+
+    with autotune(True):
+        tuned = _run(p, use_bias)
+    assert _sqnr_db(expected, tuned.float()) > 40.0
+    # The tuning call's own M is its largest bucket, stored under the cache
+    # key of M. Cake is measured there only when every M of that key has a
+    # route (the key 128 holds M=65..127, which do not).
+    cake_runner = gemm_svdquant._cake_nvfp4_svdquant_gemm_runner(None)
+    inputs = _runner_inputs(p, use_bias, tuned)
+    problem = gemm_svdquant._cake_nvfp4_svdquant_problem(inputs)
+    listed = _key_admits(m, problem, None)
+    if m <= 128:
+        assert not listed
+    offered = cake_runner.get_valid_tactics(inputs, _profile(m))
+    assert offered == ([0] if listed else [])
+    # Tuning measured Cake at the bucket of M exactly when its key lists Cake;
+    # either runner may win.
+    assert ((_CAKE_RUNNER, m) in profiled) == listed
+    assert (_CUTLASS_RUNNER, m) in profiled
+    failed = AutoTuner.get().stats.failed_tactics
+    assert f"{_OP}::{_CAKE_RUNNER}" not in failed
+
+    # Replay outside the tuning context with whichever runner won. A failed
+    # Cake measurement would leave the comparison incomplete and uncached.
+    # Outside tuning Cake is listed only while the tuner holds a Cake winner.
+    replay = _run(p, use_bias)
+    assert _sqnr_db(expected, replay.float()) > 40.0
+    runners, (winner, tactic) = svdquant_choices[-1]
+    cake_held = _holds_cake_winner(AutoTuner.get())
+    assert cake_held or type(winner).__name__ != _CAKE_RUNNER
+    expected = (
+        [_CUTLASS_RUNNER, _CAKE_RUNNER] if listed and cake_held else [_CUTLASS_RUNNER]
+    )
+    assert _runner_names(runners) == expected
+    assert any(winner is runner for runner in runners)
+    assert not (winner is runners[0] and tactic == -1)

+def test_stream_k_workspace_is_owned_by_the_current_stream():
+    # The stream-K tail's FP32 partials and generation flags belong to the current
+    # CUDA stream: launches on one stream are ordered and share them, launches on
+    # different streams are not ordered and get their own.
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("CUDA device required")
+    device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
+    # A slice count no plan uses, so these flags are first allocated here.
+    floats, flags, slices = 3 * 128 * 192, 96, 1009
+    contexts = [
+        torch.cuda.current_stream(device),
+        torch.cuda.Stream(device),
+        torch.cuda.Stream(device),
+    ]
+    buffers = []
+    for stream in contexts:
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            ws, fl = cb._stream_k_workspace(device, floats, flags, slices)
+            # Smaller requests and an index-less device reuse the same storage.
+            again = cb._stream_k_workspace(
+                torch.device("cuda"), floats // 2, flags // 2, slices
+            )
+        assert ws.dtype == torch.float32 and fl.dtype == torch.uint32
+        assert ws.numel() >= floats and fl.numel() >= flags
+        assert again[0].data_ptr() == ws.data_ptr()
+        assert again[1].data_ptr() == fl.data_ptr()
+        buffers.append((ws, fl))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    for _, fl in buffers:
+        assert not fl.view(torch.int32).any(), "flags not zero on first allocation"
+    ptrs = [t.data_ptr() for pair in buffers for t in pair]
+    assert len(set(ptrs)) == len(ptrs), "streams share stream-K scratch"
+
+    # Grown flags restart from zero in new storage.
+    stream = contexts[1]
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        _, fl = cb._stream_k_workspace(device, floats, flags, slices)
+        fl.view(torch.int32).fill_(7)
+        bigger = fl.numel() + 1
+        _, grown = cb._stream_k_workspace(device, floats, bigger, slices)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert grown.numel() >= bigger and grown.data_ptr() != fl.data_ptr()
+    assert not grown.view(torch.int32).any()
+
+
+# (m, n, k) rows whose default plan runs the stream-K tail of the static 2-CTA
+# schedule at some SM count; the test runs the first one this GPU plans with it.
+_STREAM_K_ROWS = (
+    (2048, 7168, 16384),
+    (2048, 7168, 18432),
+    (512, 8192, 28672),
+    (257, 8192, 28672),
+    (8192, 1536, 7168),
+)
+
+
+def _stream_k_row(device):
+    """The first :data:`_STREAM_K_ROWS` row whose mm_fp4 plan (default tactic, then
+    the GEMM-alone tactic, as :func:`cb._gemm_prepared`) keeps the stream-K tail."""
+    arch, sm_count = cb._device_arch(device), cb._sm_count(device)
+    for m, n, k in _STREAM_K_ROWS:
+        plan = cb.gemm_plan(m, n, k, False, arch, sm_count)
+        if (alone := cb.gemm_alone_tactic(plan)) is not None:
+            plan = cb.gemm_plan(m, n, k, False, arch, sm_count, tactic=alone)
+        if plan.stream_k:
+            return m, n, k
+    pytest.skip(f"no stream-K row on {arch} with {sm_count} SMs")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.timeout(600)
+def test_stream_k_launches_on_two_streams_match_serial_launches():
+    # Stream-K launches on two streams, not ordered with each other, each use their
+    # own partials and flags: every output equals the output of a launch alone.
+    device = _require_program()
+    m, n, k = _stream_k_row(device)
+    _, _, a_fp4, a_sf, alpha, w_fp4, w_sf, _, _ = _operands(
+        m, n, k, torch.bfloat16, device, seed=700
+    )
+
+    def run(out):
+        return mm_fp4(
+            a_fp4, w_fp4.T, a_sf, w_sf.T, alpha, torch.bfloat16, out, backend="cake"
+        )
+
+    serial = run(torch.empty((m, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device))
+    again = run(torch.empty_like(serial))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+    plan = cb._gemm_prepared(m, n, k, False, device.index)[0]
+    assert plan.stream_k, plan.kernel_key
+    ref = (_dequantize(a_fp4, a_sf) @ _dequantize(w_fp4, w_sf).T) * alpha[:, None]
+    _assert_matches(serial, ref)
+    deterministic = torch.equal(serial, again)
+
+    iterations = 20
+    streams = (torch.cuda.Stream(device), torch.cuda.Stream(device))
+    outs = [torch.full_like(serial, float("nan")) for _ in range(2 * iterations)]
+    scratch = []
+    for stream in streams:
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(device))
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            ws, fl = cb._stream_k_workspace(
+                device, plan.sk_workspace_floats, plan.sk_flag_words, plan.sk_slices
+            )
+        scratch += [ws.data_ptr(), fl.data_ptr()]
+    assert len(set(scratch)) == len(scratch), "streams share stream-K scratch"
+    # Alternate the streams without synchronising them, so their launches overlap.
+    for i in range(iterations):
+        for j, stream in enumerate(streams):
+            with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+                run(outs[2 * i + j])
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+
+    for index, out in enumerate(outs):
+        if deterministic:
+            assert torch.equal(out, serial), f"launch {index} (stream {index % 2})"
+        else:
+            _assert_matches(out, ref)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.timeout(600)
+def test_stream_k_graphs_replay_in_any_order():
+    # Graphs captured on one stream, with no eager launch on that stream before, each
+    # own zeroed stream-K flags: the graph captured second replays first and both
+    # replay concurrently on two streams, and every output equals an eager launch.
+    device = _require_program()
+    m, n, k = _stream_k_row(device)
+    _, _, a_fp4, a_sf, alpha, w_fp4, w_sf, _, _ = _operands(
+        m, n, k, torch.bfloat16, device, seed=701
+    )
+
+    def run(out):
+        return mm_fp4(
+            a_fp4, w_fp4.T, a_sf, w_sf.T, alpha, torch.bfloat16, out, backend="cake"
+        )
+
+    eager = run(torch.empty((m, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device))
+    again = run(torch.empty_like(eager))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+    assert cb._gemm_prepared(m, n, k, False, device.index)[0].stream_k
+    ref = (_dequantize(a_fp4, a_sf) @ _dequantize(w_fp4, w_sf).T) * alpha[:, None]
+    _assert_matches(eager, ref)
+    deterministic = torch.equal(eager, again)
+
+    capture_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device)
+    outs = [torch.full_like(eager, float("nan")) for _ in range(2)]
+    graphs = [torch.cuda.CUDAGraph() for _ in range(2)]
+    for graph, out in zip(graphs, outs, strict=True):
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=capture_stream):
+            run(out)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+
+    def check():
+        for index, out in enumerate(outs):
+            if deterministic:
+                assert torch.equal(out, eager), f"graph {index}"
+            else:
+                _assert_matches(out, ref)
+            out.fill_(float("nan"))
+
+    graphs[1].replay()
+    graphs[0].replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+    check()
+    streams = (torch.cuda.Stream(device), torch.cuda.Stream(device))
+    for _ in range(10):
+        for graph, stream in zip(graphs, streams, strict=True):
+            stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream(device))
+            with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+                graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
+        check()
+

Replies to the two review findings outside the diff (head bc572df83):

**Keep the Cake runner list identical across a tuning group** (`gemm_base.py`, `_cake_bf16_bmm_offered`): confirmed and fixed. While a tuner tunes under an autotune process group (`set_autotune_process_group`), `bmm_bf16`, `mm_nvfp4_svdquant` and per-token `mm_fp4` no longer list the Cake candidate, so every rank builds the runner list that main builds (`_cake_group_tuning` in `gemm_base.py`, and `_heuristic_func_nvfp4_svdquant`). Serving with the group still set is unchanged, because the group check runs only in tuning mode. A cached non-Cake winner from group tuning is found before an older Cake key, because Cake is always the last runner. New tests record the runner names passed to the group check for an M that offers Cake and an M that does not, and require them to be equal: `test_bmm_bf16_group_tuning_plans_the_same_runners_for_every_m` and `test_group_tuning_plans_the_same_runners_for_every_m` (svdquant). The docs now state that group tuning does not measure Cake.

**Do not replay a swap-AB Cake winner for an M that runs the dispatcher** (`gemm_base.py:2369`): not changed. The top-bucket fallback (`search_cache` → `_top_tuned_profile`) is a general autotuner property on main. It replays every runner's winner above the tuned range, including CUTLASS, cuDNN and the CuTe DSL swap-AB tactics. `CakeBf16BmmRunner` has one tactic (`-1`) and routes on the actual shape. The swap-AB program runs only on its exact row, and every other shape runs the dispatcher. Both compute the exact product. The call site lists Cake only for operands that Cake serves at the actual M. The replay is therefore always correct; only its speed was not measured at that M, as for the other runners. Making replay program-exact needs profile-aware runtime validation in the autotuner, which is a separate change.
